newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest milling wheat, maize futures close firmer.
newsitem.headline: Budapest milling wheat, maize futures close firmer.

text.p: Milling wheat futures extended gains on the Budapest Commodity Exchange on Tuesday, driving maize futures higher, too, traders said.
"The milling wheat buying of the past week continued and many speculators joined as buyers," said Swap Ugynoki Kft's Janos Szojka.
He added that buying had been triggered by purchases from two major brokerages.
"Two main brokerages, behind whom mills and exporters are believed to stand, began purchases and they were followed by others," Szojka said.
The most actively traded position was August, which rose by 330 forints to 20,440 forints per tonne.
September gained 300 to 20.700 and December 400 forints to 22,400. October wheat registered one deal just before the close and fell 30 forints to 21,050.
Trade concentrated on the 1997 crop, fuelled by expectations that export markets could be found for the crop above current prices, traders said.
Maize futures were buoyed partly by positive sentiment in wheat, partly because March futures were settled last week at a relatively high level of 18,500 forints, traders added.
Traders said large carry-over stocks from 1996 were likely to put maize prices under pressure in the longer term.
